title: Car Rental Companies: Hertz, Avis, Enterprise & More
description: A guide to the major car rental companies: Hertz, Avis, Enterprise, SIXT, Europcar, Budget, Alamo, National, Thrifty and Dollar, and who owns which brand.
intro: Most of the big rental brands belong to a handful of groups. Here’s who’s who, with links to each brand’s site in the USA, UK and Europe.

image.alt: Rows of rental cars in the car hire parking area at Florence Airport

blocks.title: Rental brands
blocks.intro: Open a brand’s own site for your region. Loyalty members often get faster pick-up and member rates.

blocks.title: Comparison sites and brokers
blocks.intro: Brokers and metasearch sites compare many suppliers, including local companies you may not know.

sections.html:
• Enterprise Mobility: Enterprise, National and Alamo.
  • Avis Budget Group: Avis and Budget (and Zipcar car sharing).
  • Hertz: Hertz, Dollar and Thrifty.
  • Sixt SE: SIXT, a German company with a large European network and a growing presence in the US.
  • Europcar Mobility Group: Europcar, plus low-cost brands in Europe.

In some countries brands are run by local franchise partners, so service and policies can differ from country to country.

Booking direct with a brand makes it easy to use loyalty programmes and deal with one company if plans change. Brokers such as Rentalcars.com or Discover Cars compare many suppliers at once, including local firms, and sometimes find lower prices. With a broker, your contract is still with the rental company at the desk, so read both sets of terms.

faqs.q: Are Alamo, National and Enterprise the same company?
faqs.a: They’re separate brands owned by the same group, Enterprise Mobility. Prices, policies and loyalty programmes differ between them.

faqs.q: Is it better to book with a broker or direct?
faqs.a: Neither is always cheaper. Compare both: brokers search many suppliers at once, while brands may offer member rates and simpler changes.
